source.title: Rites of passage of the engram: reconsolidation and the lingering consolidation hypothesis.

confidence_rationale: Strong source; grounds the 'contested' (labile-on-reactivation) state but explicitly bounds it -- reconsolidation as time-limited lingering consolidation, mostly fresh memories, blockade does not induce permanent amnesia. The labile state is real but narrower than an indefinitely re-writable 'contested' slot, hence mixed.
failure_signatures: Reconsolidation occurs mostly in relatively fresh memories and blockade of reconsolidation does not induce permanent amnesia -- so a 'contested' lifecycle state cannot be modelled as an always-available, indefinitely re-writable mode; the window is bounded and may be a tail of the original consolidation rather than a recapitulated process.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Reactivated memories can re-enter a state sensitive to amnestic agents (reconsolidation), but the authors argue this reflects 'lingering consolidation' -- a tail of the original stabilisation, occurring mainly in fresh memories -- rather than a full recapitulation of consolidation, and its blockade does not produce permanent amnesia.
mapping.ree_translation: Biological warrant for the 'contested' state in MECH-391's lifecycle: a stored trace is not permanently inert -- reactivation can return it to a labile, re-writable condition. This is the substrate analogue of a memory leaving a settled state and re-entering one where it can be updated or challenged.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper deliberately bounds the phenomenon: the labile window is time-limited and may be a lingering tail of initial consolidation, not a fully recurrent process. So it grounds that a 'contested' state EXISTS but cautions against modelling it as an unbounded, always-on re-write mode -- the REE state must carry an eligibility window, not a standing invitation.
mapping.source_context: Review/synthesis of rodent reconsolidation experiments (amnestic-agent blockade paradigms).

confidence_components.notes: Mixed by design: grounds the contested state's existence while problematising an over-broad reading of it.
